actual_scope: Prove the minimum number of binary address bits for an affine A5 action whose extension to the full F2[A5] algebra is injective. Covers all affine representations, including nonsplit modules and actions without a fixed point.
scope_change_reason: Take the unclaimed Open next question 2 of Nick Petalas's PR5114, after its eight-bit construction claim was completed and released. This is a universal address-realization obstruction, not another paid-word search or a replay of the predecessor's construction.
bottleneck_link: The theorem rules out reducing the existing carrier's 256-address footprint by choosing another binary affine representation. It is a scoped interface result; no physical tariff, native supplier or kappa gain follows.
stop_rule: Stop at the first complete minimum theorem or smaller construction; if the small-module completeness reduction fails, record the precise gap without claiming a universal minimum. No word search, physical caller campaign or frontier change.
evidence: README proof reduces every relevant module to two explicit universal extensions. Independent finite algebra implementation certifies the quotient F2 x M2(F4) x M4(F2), rank25, and radical power dimensions 35,27,17,9,0. Exact permutation-action ranks52 and34 yield nonzero annihilators. Their preservation through subquotients and affine homogenization proves the seven-bit obstruction; PR5114 supplies the matching eight-bit regular orbit. Author-checked, no independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.
